title: Support separate browser profiles for multiple Amazon accounts
body:
## Problem

The MCP process caches one persistent Playwright browser context and currently always uses the same profile directory. Running separate MCP instances for personal and business Amazon accounts therefore makes both instances contend for or share one authenticated profile. Playwright does not allow simultaneous browser instances to use the same user-data directory.

## Resolution

Allow each process to select its profile directory with `AMAZON_ORDERS_BROWSER_DATA_DIR`, while retaining the existing default when the variable is unset. The implementation is already proposed in PR #2.

## Implementation context

- File: `src/index.ts`
- Pattern: resolve the module-level browser data directory from the environment before the first `launchPersistentContext` call.
- Compatibility: preserve the existing default directory for users who do not set the variable.
- Scope: no dependency, MCP tool-schema, or browser-lifecycle changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- An unset variable uses the existing persistent profile directory.
- Distinct configured values are passed to Playwright as distinct user-data directories, allowing independent account sessions.
- Existing startup, typecheck, lint, and test behavior remains unchanged.

## Verification

Run `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test`; inspect the `launchPersistentContext` argument for configured and unconfigured processes.

Implementation: PR #2.

title: Restore SonarCloud authentication and supported scan action
body:
## Problem

The `SonarCloud Analysis` job is failing before analysis on both release PR #9 and released `main` commit `34c3464d4d3d53cfb79ac6c2ed1dbf0a97cc5677`. The scanner reports:

> Failed to query JRE metadata. Please check `sonar.token` or `SONAR_TOKEN`.

All repository-owned lint, typecheck, test, integration, build, and release jobs passed. This is an authentication/configuration failure rather than a source-analysis finding, but it leaves the overall `Code Quality` workflow red.

Evidence:

- Released-main run: https://github.com/marcusquinn/amazon-order-history-csv-download-mcp/actions/runs/33810900427
- Release PR run: https://github.com/marcusquinn/amazon-order-history-csv-download-mcp/actions/runs/33810432142
- The workflow also warns that `SonarSource/sonarcloud-github-action@master` is deprecated.

## Scope

- Verify that the SonarCloud project named by `sonar-project.properties` still exists and the organization/project binding is correct.
- Rotate or replace the repository `SONAR_TOKEN` using GitHub/SonarCloud secret-management controls; never print or commit the token.
- Update `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` from the deprecated wrapper action to the supported SonarQube scan action, pinning an independently verified immutable revision rather than copying a scanner suggestion blindly.
- Replace the actionlint-blocking `codecov/codecov-action@v3` reference in the same workflow with a supported, immutable action and reviewed CLI version while preserving its upload policy.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior for genuine scanner or quality-gate failures. Do not solve this by making the analysis silently optional.

## Relevant files

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`, especially the `sonarcloud` job around lines 56-68
- `sonar-project.properties`

## Verification

- Rerun `Code Quality` for a reviewed commit and show `SonarCloud Analysis` completing successfully.
- Confirm SonarCloud received analysis for the exact tested commit and reports no new bug or vulnerability regression.
- Confirm workflow logs and repository history disclose no credential value.
- Run the repository lint, typecheck, test, and build gates after any workflow edit.

## Dispatch constraint

Maintainer-only token rotation was completed on 2026-09-03, and rerunning released-main Code Quality run `33810900427` proved SonarCloud authentication succeeds. The workflow migration must not receive or expose the token value.

title: Fix bounded order ranges spanning calendar years
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Origin

- Source: the still-valid cross-year portion of PR #3 after its APX transaction and browser-recovery work was superseded by #6 and #8.
- Evidence: Amazon order-history URLs accept one `year-YYYY` filter at a time, while the current `fetchOrders` path builds and visits only one list URL. A bounded range spanning calendar years can therefore omit every order outside that selected/default year.
- Collision check: no matching issue exists; open PR #1 improves bounded date filtering but does not enumerate every year in a cross-year range.

## What

Make every order-list tool backed by `fetchOrders` return the complete inclusive date range when `start_date` and `end_date` cross calendar-year boundaries.

Preserve these behaviors:

- Date bounds override `year`, matching the public tool description.
- Both bounds: visit each inclusive calendar year, newest year first, then retain only orders inside the inclusive bounds.
- Start only: visit from the current year back through the start year and retain orders on or after the start date.
- End only: visit the end-date year and retain orders on or before the end date.
- No date bounds: preserve the existing explicit-year/current-year behavior.
- Reject invalid dates and inverted ranges before browser navigation with a structured `FetchOrdersResult.errors` entry.

## Why

The current path passes dates to `getOrderListUrl`, but `AmazonPlugin.getOrderListUrl` can express only one `timeFilter` year and ignores custom bounds. Users can request a valid cross-year range and silently receive incomplete exports. Applying `maxOrders` before date filtering can also let out-of-range rows consume the limit.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `src/tools/fetch-orders.ts`
- Focused Jest coverage under `tests/` using existing test infrastructure; create the narrowest suitable test file if no current file covers `fetchOrders` orchestration.
- Change `src/amazon/adapter.ts` only if a minimal reusable year-filter adjustment is required; its current `year-YYYY` URL behavior is otherwise the reference pattern.

### Complete Write Surface

- In `fetchOrders`, replace the single navigation/extraction block around the current order-list URL with a bounded year plan and per-year pagination.
- Filter each page’s extracted headers before appending them to `result.orders` and before evaluating `maxOrders`.
- For bounded requests, exclude headers with missing or invalid dates and add one bounded summary error rather than allowing them through or emitting one error per row.
- Preserve newest-first result order and stop all year/page traversal as soon as the filtered result reaches `maxOrders`.
- Keep detail, invoice, item, shipment, and transaction enrichment after header collection so each accepted order is enriched once.

### Implementation Steps

1. Parse and validate date bounds once before the first navigation.
2. Derive the ordered year list according to the behaviors above.
3. For each year, call the existing platform URL builder with that explicit year, navigate, verify authentication, and paginate using the existing helpers.
4. Apply inclusive date filtering to each page before append/limit decisions.
5. Keep progress reporting coherent across year transitions and preserve existing early-return error behavior.
6. Add focused regression coverage for a range crossing December/January, limit handling, missing/invalid order dates, start-only, end-only, inverted dates, and unchanged single-year behavior.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Compare calendar dates without introducing locale/timezone off-by-one exclusions.
- Do not merge PR #3 wholesale; its branch conflicts and its previous implementation had verified limit/filter and open-ended-range defects.
- Do not add a new test runner, browser-download requirement, or test-only production interface.
- Preserve all supported Amazon regions and existing legacy pagination behavior.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- Confirm the current references remain at `src/tools/fetch-orders.ts` order-list orchestration and `src/amazon/adapter.ts` year-filter URL construction.
- Run `npm run typecheck`.
- Run `npm run lint`.
- Run `npm test`.
- Run `npm run build`.
- Run `git diff --check`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A bounded range spanning two or more years visits every inclusive year and returns only in-range orders.
- [ ] `maxOrders` counts only valid in-range orders and stops traversal once that filtered limit is reached.
- [ ] Missing or unparseable order dates cannot leak into bounded results.
- [ ] Start-only, end-only, explicit-year, invalid-date, and inverted-range behavior matches the contract above.
- [ ] Result ordering remains newest first and enrichment runs once per accepted order.
- [ ] Existing required lint, typecheck, test, build, and diff checks pass without new infrastructure.

title: Unify modern item extraction to preserve row-level quantities
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `amazon invoice item quantity shared extractor systemic fix` → 0 hits — no relevant prior lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 recent commits / 0 merged PRs / 1 open PR touch the target behavior; PR #1 is the reviewed source proposal and has no competing implementation on `main`.
- [x] File refs verified: `src/amazon/extractors/invoice.ts`, `src/amazon/extractors/items.ts`, and `src/tools/fetch-orders.ts` exist at current `HEAD`; all cited flows were inspected.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — architecture and behavior are decided, but consolidating three extraction paths requires bounded implementation judgment.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — this interactive session will implement and verify the issue after it is created and claimed.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-03
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive maintainer session
- **Conversation context:** Maintainer review of PR #1 confirmed that mixed-quantity invoice rows are bound incorrectly in multiple public order paths. The contributed row-scoping fix is directionally correct but repairs only one duplicate extractor.

## What

Create one shared extractor for modern Amazon `[data-component="purchasedItems"]` markup, scope item fields to each `.a-fixed-left-grid` row, and make invoice, detail-page, bulk-order, and single-order flows consume that implementation instead of maintaining independent container-level parsing.

## Why

Amazon omits `.od-item-view-qty` for quantity-one items. Pairing container-wide title, price, and quantity lists by index therefore assigns badges to the wrong product when one shipment contains multiple rows. The same assumption currently appears in `invoice.ts`, `items.ts`, and the single-order branch of `fetch-orders.ts`; repairing only one copy leaves accounting exports inconsistent across MCP tools.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The owning boundary and expected behavior are resolved, but the shared intermediate type, fallback preservation, and caller adaptation require normal multi-file judgment.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Issue-first implementation keeps the source PR's partial patch from becoming an implementation anchor.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Discovery and file verification were completed against current `main`.
- **Verification run:** Existing source and the PR #1 regression fixture were inspected; implementation checks remain pending.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Re-check if another PR changes any of the three extraction paths before push.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: src/amazon/extractors/data-component-items.ts` — own row discovery and extraction of the common modern-markup item fields.
- `EDIT: src/amazon/extractors/invoice.ts:540-748` — replace its container-wide strategy with the shared extractor and map the shared result to `InvoiceItem`.
- `EDIT: src/amazon/extractors/items.ts:145-320` — make Strategy 4 consume the shared extractor while preserving `Item`, seller, URL, and fallback behavior.
- `EDIT: src/tools/fetch-orders.ts:142-444` — remove the duplicate single-order parser and use the canonical invoice extraction result.
- `NEW: tests/integration/fixtures/invoice-multi-item-qty.html` — represent one singleton plus a multi-row shipment where only the middle row has quantity two.
- `NEW: tests/integration/invoice-items.test.ts` — exercise the shared extractor and public single-order mapping with existing Jest/Playwright infrastructure where practical.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `extractFromInvoice` in `src/amazon/extractors/invoice.ts`; Strategy 4 and `extractItems` in `src/amazon/extractors/items.ts`; single- and multi-order orchestration in `src/tools/fetch-orders.ts`; adapter calls through `src/amazon/adapter.ts` remain API-compatible.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** No persistent state is written. The change only constructs in-memory `InvoiceItem` and `Item` records.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `tests/integration/order-list.test.ts`, `tests/unit/core/money.test.ts`, and the repository `typecheck`, `lint`, `test`, and `build` scripts. Add focused regression coverage because incorrect quantities alter accounting totals and the current paths have no mixed-row fixture.
- **Schemas/config:** Public MCP schemas and CSV columns are unchanged; `Item` and `InvoiceItem` contracts remain unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `dist/` is generated by `npm run build` and must not be committed.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because extraction is stateless and the corrected association applies on the next invocation.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** N/A because a normal PR revert restores the prior strategies and no persistent data requires cleanup.

### Implementation Steps

1. Introduce a shared modern-markup result type and extractor. Iterate each `purchasedItems` container, then each item row inside it; bind title, href/ASIN, price, condition, frequency, and quantity within that row. Read seller at the container level only where Amazon shares it across rows.
2. Preserve compatibility for a legacy container containing exactly one title but no `.a-fixed-left-grid`: treat the container as one item scope. Never positionally pair sparse quantity badges with multiple titles.
3. Adapt `invoice.ts` and `items.ts` to their existing public result types without changing fallback strategy ordering.
4. Replace `fetch-orders.ts` single-order inline parsing with the canonical invoice extraction path so amounts, addresses, payments, and items are extracted once through one owner.
5. Add the mixed-quantity fixture and focused assertions for item identity, quantity, price, seller, and the quantity-one default. Ensure unavailable Playwright does not turn the regression into a false passing assertion; use an installed browser path when the repository's existing test setup supports it without new infrastructure.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Extraction is page-local and sequential; no shared mutable state or race is introduced.
- **Migration/rollback:** No migration. Reverting the PR restores the old extraction logic.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Public interfaces and CSV output shape remain stable. Legacy table/link/text fallbacks retain their current ordering.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Re-running extraction on the same DOM produces the same records; no write or retry semantics change.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** A malformed row is skipped without discarding valid sibling rows, matching existing tolerant extraction. A multi-title container without identifiable per-item rows must fall through rather than invent quantity associations.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm test -- --runInBand tests/integration/invoice-items.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run build
git diff --check
```

- **Surface mapping:** The focused integration test proves row identity and quantity behavior; typecheck covers shared result adaptation; lint/build cover all production callers; `git diff --check` guards patch integrity.
- **Broad verification trigger:** The extractor is shared by multiple MCP order and export paths, so run the repository's existing full `npm test` before PR readiness.
- **Broad verification command:** `npm test`

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `npm test -- --runInBand tests/integration/invoice-items.test.ts`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: share modern item extraction`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: `npm test`

### Files Scope

- `src/amazon/extractors/data-component-items.ts`
- `src/amazon/extractors/invoice.ts`
- `src/amazon/extractors/items.ts`
- `src/tools/fetch-orders.ts`
- `tests/integration/fixtures/invoice-multi-item-qty.html`
- `tests/integration/invoice-items.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A multi-item `purchasedItems` container returns every item and binds a sparse quantity badge only to its own `.a-fixed-left-grid` row.
- [ ] Quantity-one rows without badges remain quantity one; their title, price, condition, and frequency are not borrowed from sibling rows.
- [ ] Invoice, detail-page, bulk-order, and single-order flows use the shared modern-markup extractor instead of separate container-wide implementations.
- [ ] Existing fallback layouts and public `Item`/`InvoiceItem`/CSV contracts remain unchanged.
- [ ] Focused regression coverage, typecheck, lint, build, full tests, and `git diff --check` pass without adding a runner or dependency.

## Context & Decisions

- PR #1 supplies useful evidence and a passing row-scoped fixture, but its implementation is partial and remains unmerged.
- The systemic owning boundary is modern data-component item extraction, not a one-off quantity adjustment in one caller.
- Cross-year date filtering is tracked separately in #11. Invoice PDF download remains a separate feature because it has independent validation and file-write concerns.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** None.
- **Blocks:** A focused replacement for the quantity-attribution portion of PR #1.
- **External:** No credentials or new services; live Amazon verification is optional supporting evidence, not required for deterministic fixture coverage.

title: Make Docker CI fail truthfully with Compose v2
body:
## What

Make the Docker CI job execute the repository Docker test through Compose v2 and report its real result instead of succeeding after the test command fails.

## Why

The post-merge `main` Tests run `33816244312`, Docker job `100848921222`, reported overall success even though `npm run test:docker` failed immediately with `sh: 1: docker-compose: not found` and exit code 127. `.github/workflows/test.yml` masks the failure with `continue-on-error: true`, so the current green job is a false positive.

## Evidence

- Commit: `9ce9e4711f0c04390a289772790a0746fa36e9cc`
- Workflow run: `33816244312`
- Job: `100848921222`
- Observed command: `cd tests/docker && docker-compose run --rm test`
- Observed result: `docker-compose` is unavailable on the Ubuntu 24.04 hosted runner; the step exits 127 while the job remains successful.
- Duplicate discovery found no recent commit, merged PR, open PR, or open issue covering these target files and keywords.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
gh run view 33816244312 --repo marcusquinn/amazon-order-history-csv-download-mcp --job 100848921222 --log
```

**Actual output**:

```text
> cd tests/docker && docker-compose run --rm test
sh: 1: docker-compose: not found
Error: Process completed with exit code 127.
```

The workflow nevertheless records the Docker job as successful.

**Expected output**:

The hosted runner invokes Compose v2, executes the container test, and the Docker job reports that command’s terminal status.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `.github/workflows/test.yml:52-60` runs `npm run test:docker` in the hosted Docker job and sets `continue-on-error: true`.
- **Call chain**: Tests workflow → `npm run test:docker` → `package.json` invokes unavailable `docker-compose` → exit 127 → `continue-on-error` converts the failed step into an overall successful job.
- **Integrated verification**: hosted push run `33816244312`, job `100848921222`, exercises this exact workflow and records both the exit-127 annotation and successful job conclusion.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `package.json` — update the `test:docker` script to invoke the available Compose v2 subcommand.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — stop masking Docker test failures.
- `tests/docker/` — inspect only if the now-executed existing test reveals a genuine compatibility defect; do not redesign the harness.

### Complete Write Surface

In `package.json`, replace:

```json
"test:docker": "cd tests/docker && docker-compose run --rm test"
```

with:

```json
"test:docker": "cd tests/docker && docker compose run --rm test"
```

In `.github/workflows/test.yml`, remove this line from the Docker test step:

```yaml
continue-on-error: true
```

### Implementation Steps

1. Apply the two exact changes above.
2. Run the existing Docker test with Compose v2 and repair only directly exposed repository compatibility failures.
3. Verify the GitHub Docker job records failure for a failing test and success only when the container test completes successfully.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Do not add another `continue-on-error`, shell fallback, or unconditional success path.
- Preserve `docker compose run --rm test` cleanup behavior.
- Do not add a new test runner, mock, fixture, or CI service.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- `docker compose version`
- `npm run test:docker`
- `actionlint .github/workflows/test.yml`
- `npx prettier --check package.json .github/workflows/test.yml`
- `git diff --check`
- Hosted Docker CI job completes with a truthful terminal status.

## Tier

`tier:simple`: the two required edits are exact and reversible; verification uses the existing Docker workflow.

## PR Conventions

Use `Resolves #NNN` for this leaf issue.

title: Migrate GitHub actions off deprecated Node 20 runtimes
body:
## What

Migrate every GitHub workflow use of `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-node@v4` to supported Node 24-based releases, pinned to independently verified immutable commit SHAs.

## Why

Current GitHub-hosted runs emit deprecation warnings that both actions target the retired Node 20 action runtime and are being forcibly executed with Node 24. Removing the warnings before compatibility enforcement changes prevents avoidable workflow breakage and keeps action supply-chain pins explicit.

## Evidence

- Post-merge Tests run `33816244312` on commit `9ce9e4711f0c04390a289772790a0746fa36e9cc` warns in every checkout/setup step that Node 20 is deprecated and the action is being forced onto Node 24.
- Runner version `2.337.0` exceeds the minimum documented for Node 24-based action releases.
- Exact call-site sweep found 8 `actions/checkout@v4` and 5 `actions/setup-node@v4` uses across three workflow files.
- Duplicate discovery and GitHub issue/PR searches found no existing work covering this migration.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
gh run watch 33816244312 --repo marcusquinn/amazon-order-history-csv-download-mcp --exit-status
```

**Actual output**:

```text
Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4.
```

**Expected output**:

All checkout and setup-node steps use supported Node 24-based action releases without action-runtime deprecation warnings.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`, and `.github/workflows/release.yml` invoke the two v4 actions in hosted workflows.
- **Call chain**: workflow event → v4 JavaScript action metadata selects Node 20 runtime → GitHub runner forces Node 24 and emits the warning.
- **Integrated verification**: hosted run `33816244312` executes the affected production workflow call sites and emits the warnings.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`

### Complete Write Surface

Replace all 8 checkout v4 references and all 5 setup-node v4 references. Resolve the current upstream supported release tags at implementation time, verify tag-to-commit provenance and GitHub verification, then pin each action to its full immutable commit SHA with a trailing release-tag comment. No other workflow action requires a change unless direct hosted-run evidence shows the same Node 20 warning.

### Implementation Steps

1. Verify the current official Node 24-based release for each action and its minimum runner requirement.
2. Verify each release tag resolves to the intended commit and record the provenance evidence in the PR.
3. Replace every call site from the sweep with one consistent immutable pin per action.
4. Preserve all existing workflow triggers, app-level Node test matrix values, cache inputs, permissions, and step behavior.
5. Validate both pull-request and push workflow runs.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- The matrix entries `node-version: [18, 20, 22]` test this project’s supported application runtimes; do not remove or alter them as part of the JavaScript action-runtime migration.
- Do not use floating major tags in the final workflow.
- Do not broaden token permissions or change release behavior.
- Coordinate with issue #16 if both changes touch `.github/workflows/test.yml`; rebase rather than duplicating or overwriting its Docker CI fix.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml`
- `npx prettier --check .github/workflows/*.yml`
- `git diff --check`
- All PR workflow jobs pass.
- A subsequent hosted workflow run has no Node 20 action-runtime warning for checkout or setup-node.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: file scope and acceptance are fixed, but the worker must verify current upstream releases and immutable commit provenance before editing.

## PR Conventions

Use `Resolves #NNN` for this leaf issue.

title: Add validated Amazon invoice PDF download tool
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# Add validated Amazon invoice PDF download tool

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `Amazon invoice PDF download validation safe output path Playwright` → 0 hits — no relevant stored lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: 6 recent commits touched candidate paths / 0 merged feature PRs / 0 open feature PRs implement invoice PDF download; closed PR #1 is the source proposal, while PRs #13 and #15 superseded only its unrelated bug fixes.
- [x] File refs verified: 8 existing references checked at `90391bd`; all are present on current `main`, and both proposed new-file parent directories exist.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — the behavior and safety boundaries are decided, but fixture selectors and bounded helper decomposition require normal implementation judgment.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the stale implementation in closed PR #1 must not anchor work against current `main`.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-04
- **Created by:** AI DevOps interactive maintainer session
- **Conversation context:** Maintainer review of PR #1 accepted invoice PDF download as an in-scope standalone feature but declined the mixed, conflicting PR. This issue preserves the feature with the correctness and file-safety requirements identified by that review.

## What

Add a `download_amazon_invoice` MCP tool that accepts `order_id`, `region`, and optional `output_path`, opens the authenticated Amazon order-summary print page for that order, positively verifies that the loaded document is the requested invoice, renders an A4 PDF with backgrounds, and returns the saved path and byte count. Authentication redirects, wrong-order pages, Amazon error pages, render failures, and write failures must return structured MCP errors without reporting success or leaving a new partial artifact.

The default destination is `~/Downloads/amazon-{region}-invoice-{orderId}.pdf`. A caller-supplied absolute `output_path` remains supported, matching the existing export-tool contract.

## Why

Users need source invoice artifacts for bookkeeping, VAT records, and document-extraction workflows. Closed PR #1 demonstrated the useful path through `getInvoiceUrl()` and `page.pdf()`, but its generic readiness selector and swallowed timeout could save an error page as a successful invoice. Its unvalidated order ID also entered the generated filename. The feature must establish invoice identity before crossing the local file-write boundary.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Public behavior, validation rules, ownership, error policy, and verification are fixed. The worker still needs bounded judgment to choose robust selectors across supported Amazon invoice layouts and to structure the helper without duplicating existing extraction logic.

## PR Conventions

This is a leaf issue. The implementation PR body must use `Resolves #NNN`, replacing `NNN` with this issue number.

## Seeded Draft PR

- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Closed PR #1 predates the current shared invoice/item extraction and date-range architecture and contains two already-superseded objectives.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Duplicate search, target history, current source, tests, documentation, and repository scripts were inspected at `90391bd`.
- **Verification run:** Brief validation only; production checks remain for the implementation worker.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Re-run collision discovery if `src/index.ts`, `src/tools/`, or invoice extraction changes before implementation starts.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: src/tools/download-invoice.ts` — own input-safe invoice navigation, positive page verification, PDF rendering, persistent-write cleanup, and a typed result contract; reuse `getInvoiceUrl` from `src/amazon/extractors/invoice.ts:63-67`.
- `EDIT: src/tools/index.ts:1-7` — export the new tool helper through the existing barrel.
- `EDIT: src/index.ts:208-245` — register `download_amazon_invoice` beside the single-order tool with `order_id`, `region`, and optional absolute `output_path`.
- `EDIT: src/index.ts:773-860` — add the request handler beside `get_amazon_order_details`, reuse `validateRegion()` and `getPage()`, and map typed success/failure to the existing JSON text plus `isError` response shape.
- `NEW: tests/integration/invoice-download.test.ts` — cover the production helper and MCP-facing behavior with the existing Jest/Playwright conventions in `tests/integration/invoice-items.test.ts:1-120`.
- `NEW: tests/integration/fixtures/invoice-download-valid.html` — minimal invoice-specific content containing the requested order identity.
- `NEW: tests/integration/fixtures/invoice-download-error.html` — same-URL Amazon error-page shape that must never produce a PDF.
- `EDIT: README.md:204-255` — document the tool, parameters, default path, result, and failure behavior.
- `EDIT: AGENTS.md:21-30` — add the tool to the quick-reference MCP table.
- `EDIT: CHANGELOG.md:8-10` — record the new tool under `Unreleased` without changing release versions.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `src/index.ts` lists and dispatches MCP tools; MCP clients read the input schema and JSON text result. `src/tools/index.ts` exposes the helper. `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` describe the public tool.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `src/tools/download-invoice.ts` is the only new persistent writer. Validate the page first, render the PDF fully before publication, create the selected parent directory when needed, write through a sibling temporary file, rename to the final path, and remove the temporary file on every failure. Existing caller-selected files may be replaced consistently with CSV export behavior.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `tests/integration/invoice-items.test.ts` supplies the current browser-executable fallback and route-fixture pattern. `package.json:20-29` supplies integration, full test, typecheck, lint, build, and formatting commands. Add focused tests because the feature introduces a new local artifact boundary and false-success risk.
- **Schemas/config:** The MCP `Tool` schema is inline in `src/index.ts`; no Zod or external configuration schema currently owns tool arguments. Keep the schema runtime-independent and validate all externally supplied strings inside the production helper or handler.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `dist/` is generated by `npm run build` and published through the package; do not commit generated output. No core-sync mirror needs modification because the feature is Amazon-specific.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no persistent schema or stored order data changes; previously exported files require no backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** On runtime failure, delete only the attempt-specific temporary file and preserve any pre-existing final file until a complete replacement is ready. A normal PR revert removes the tool, tests, docs, and changelog entry without data migration.

### Implementation Steps

1. Define a typed `DownloadInvoiceResult` discriminated union in `src/tools/download-invoice.ts` and accept `Page`, order ID, region, and resolved output path.
2. Validate `order_id` before URL or filename construction. Accept the documented Amazon form with an alphanumeric three-character prefix and two seven-digit groups, reject separators, parent components, whitespace, overlong values, and malformed input. Encode the validated identifier when constructing the URL; update `getInvoiceUrl` only if central encoding can be proven backward-compatible for existing callers.
3. Resolve the configured Amazon domain from the validated region and navigate to the print-summary route with a bounded timeout. Reject sign-in, order-history, foreign-host, unexpected-path, and known Amazon error-banner outcomes.
4. Require positive invoice evidence before rendering: the requested order ID must appear in the document and at least one invoice-specific structure such as `purchasedItems` or `chargeSummary` must exist. Do not use generic `.a-box` as success evidence and do not swallow the readiness timeout.
5. Call `page.pdf()` without a final path so rendering completes in memory. Write the resulting non-empty buffer to an attempt-specific sibling temporary file, then publish it to the requested destination. Clean the temporary file after render/write/rename failures and return a structured error. Never delete or truncate a pre-existing final file before a complete replacement is ready.
6. In `src/index.ts`, follow the adjacent order-detail registration and handler patterns. Default to the validated Downloads filename, preserve explicit absolute output paths, and return `{status, params, path, bytes}` on success or `{status, params, error}` with `isError: true` on failure.
7. Add focused route/fixture tests for success, authentication redirect, same-URL error content, mismatched order identity, malformed order IDs including traversal text, unavailable parent/write failure, and preservation of a pre-existing final file. Assert that every failure creates no new final PDF or leaves the previous file unchanged.
8. Update README, AGENTS, and the Unreleased changelog. Do not change `VERSION` or `package.json` version; release management remains separate.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Multiple requests may target the same filename. Use unique sibling temporary names and publish only complete buffers. Cleanup must remove only the current attempt temporary file. Last successful writer may replace the destination, matching explicit export overwrite behavior.
- **Migration/rollback:** No migration. Runtime code, tests, and docs land together; a revert removes the API surface while leaving user-created PDFs untouched.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** This is additive. Existing tools and invoice extraction behavior remain unchanged. Do not refactor `extractFromInvoice` or resurrect the superseded date and quantity patches from PR #1.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Repeating the same successful request may replace the same destination with a newly rendered invoice. A failed retry must not corrupt a previous successful file.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Navigation or validation fails before rendering; rendering fails before writing; write/rename failures clean the attempt temporary file and preserve the prior destination. Errors remain local and structured so the next MCP request can retry.
- **Privacy/security:** Invoice content stays local. Do not log page HTML, cookies, payment data, or addresses. Logging the validated order ID and destination is acceptable under current tool behavior. No new network destination or credential storage is introduced.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
npm test -- --runInBand tests/integration/invoice-download.test.ts
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run build
npm test
npx prettier --check src/index.ts src/tools/download-invoice.ts src/tools/index.ts tests/integration/invoice-download.test.ts README.md AGENTS.md CHANGELOG.md
git diff --check
```

- **Surface mapping:** The focused integration command proves positive identity validation, negative page outcomes, safe filenames, and artifact cleanup; typecheck and lint cover the schema and handler; build covers publishable compilation; full tests cover the shared MCP entry point.
- Typecheck and lint prove the MCP schema, handler, and typed result integration.
- Build proves the published `dist` source compiles without committing generated files.
- Full tests are justified because `src/index.ts` is the shared MCP entry point and invoice navigation shares a browser page with existing order tools.
- Prettier and diff checks cover every edited text/source surface.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused invoice-download integration test passes with an available browser.
- [ ] Create a WIP commit before broad lint/build/full-test gates.
- [ ] Re-run the full suite after any review-triggered code change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A valid region and documented Amazon order ID produce a non-empty A4 PDF only after the requested order identity and invoice-specific content are positively verified.
- [ ] The default filename remains inside `~/Downloads`; malformed identifiers containing separators, traversal text, whitespace, or invalid structure are rejected before navigation or filesystem mutation.
- [ ] Authentication redirects, order-history redirects, foreign/unexpected destinations, same-URL error pages, mismatched order identity, readiness timeouts, render failures, and write failures return structured MCP errors and never report success.
- [ ] Failure leaves no attempt temporary file and does not corrupt or delete a pre-existing destination file.
- [ ] Explicit absolute `output_path` remains supported, parent-directory behavior is documented, and successful output reports the final path and exact byte count.
- [ ] Existing order, item, shipment, transaction, and invoice extraction behavior remains unchanged; no date-range or quantity patch from closed PR #1 is reintroduced.
- [ ] README, AGENTS, and `Unreleased` changelog documentation match the shipped schema and behavior.
- [ ] Focused integration coverage, typecheck, lint, build, full tests, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass without new dependencies or test infrastructure.

## Context & Decisions

- Closed PR #1 supplied the original user need and a useful `getInvoiceUrl` plus `page.pdf` direction, but it was not mergeable and its generic success check was unsafe.
- PR #13 already owns correct bounded date traversal; PR #15 already owns row-scoped item extraction. Those implementations are references to preserve, not work to repeat.
- Positive invoice identity is mandatory because a PDF renderer can turn any HTML response into a valid-looking artifact. Redirect checks alone are insufficient.
- Caller-selected output paths are an intentional existing product capability. Safety work applies to generated defaults, complete-write publication, and cleanup rather than restricting user-authorized destinations.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** None.
- **Blocks:** A future release may include the tool after its implementation PR merges; release publication is explicitly outside this issue.
- **External:** Requires no new service, credential, dependency, or live Amazon account for deterministic fixture coverage. Optional live-account verification may supplement but must not replace fixtures.

# Fix stale MCP server version in initialize responses

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `MCP serverInfo hardcoded version package VERSION synchronization` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 related recent commits, merged PRs, or open PRs found
- [x] File refs verified: `src/index.ts:527-532`, `package.json`, `VERSION`, and `tsconfig.json` exist at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — the behavior is fixed, but the implementation must preserve both source-tree and installed-package runtime layouts
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the isolated follow-up has no implementation changes yet

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-04
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Parent task:** #25
- **Conversation context:** The public v0.4.3 npm postflight completed an MCP `initialize` handshake but returned `serverInfo.version: 0.3.0` because the source still contains a hardcoded historical version.

## What

Make the MCP server's `initialize` response report the current package version instead of the hardcoded `0.3.0`. Prefer one canonical version source so subsequent releases cannot silently leave `serverInfo.version` stale.

## Why

Clients use MCP server metadata for diagnostics and compatibility reporting. The newly published v0.4.3 package currently identifies itself as v0.3.0 even though its package metadata, release tag, and registry version are v0.4.3.

## Reproducer

Install `amz-order-history-csv-mcp@0.4.3` from the public npm registry into an isolated project.

**Symptom command**:

```bash
node --input-type=module -e 'import { spawn } from "node:child_process"; const child = spawn("./node_modules/.bin/amz-order-history-csv-mcp", [], { stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] }); child.stdout.on("data", chunk => { process.stdout.write(chunk); child.kill("SIGTERM"); }); child.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "initialize", params: { protocolVersion: "2024-11-05", capabilities: {}, clientInfo: { name: "npm-postflight", version: "1.0.0" } } }) + "\n"); child.stdin.end();'
```

**Actual output**:

```json
{"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{"tools":{}},"serverInfo":{"name":"amazon-order-history-csv-download-mcp","version":"0.3.0"}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}
```

**Expected:** `serverInfo.version` is `0.4.3`, matching the installed package.

The public package postflight reproduced this directly, and `src/index.ts:531` contains the same hardcoded value.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The target and expected behavior are known, but the implementation must work when launched from both a repository build and an npm-installed package without depending on the caller's working directory.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: src/index.ts:527-532` — replace the hardcoded server version with the canonical package version.
- `EDIT: package.json` or build/release configuration only if required to expose that canonical version safely at runtime.
- Existing test paths are not predetermined; add focused coverage only if it is the lowest-cost way to prevent recurrence without introducing new test infrastructure.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** MCP clients read `serverInfo.version` from the response produced by the `Server` created in `src/index.ts`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `src/index.ts:527-532` is the only verified writer; `package.json` and `VERSION` are release-time version sources.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, and a stdio MCP `initialize` handshake against the built executable.
- **Schemas/config:** `tsconfig.json` uses CommonJS, `rootDir: ./src`, and `resolveJsonModule: true`; verify any package-metadata import compiles under these settings.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `dist/index.js` is generated and included in the npm archive; do not edit it directly.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none; preserve package and protocol compatibility.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the source/config change and rebuild; no persistent data is involved.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace `version: "0.3.0"` in the MCP `Server` metadata with a value derived from the canonical package version. Do not resolve metadata relative to `process.cwd()`.
2. Verify the implementation works from the repository build and from an `npm pack` artifact installed into an isolated temporary project.
3. Confirm the initialize response version equals the packed package version, then run the repository's existing lint, typecheck, test, and build gates.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** no shared mutable state; version resolution occurs during process startup.
- **Migration/rollback:** no migration; a source revert restores prior behavior.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** preserve Node `>=18.0.0`, CommonJS output, and the existing MCP protocol response shape.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated builds and launches must resolve the same version from immutable package metadata.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** fail during build or startup rather than silently returning an outdated fallback version.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- `npm run lint`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test`
- `npm run build`
- Pack and install the artifact in an isolated temporary project, send an MCP `initialize` request to `amz-order-history-csv-mcp`, and assert `serverInfo.version` equals the package version.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The built repository server reports the current package version in `serverInfo.version`.
- [ ] A freshly packed and isolated-installed package reports the same version.
- [ ] Version resolution is independent of the caller's current working directory.
- [ ] Node 18+ and CommonJS compatibility remain intact.
- [ ] Existing lint, typecheck, test, and build commands pass.
